solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Diehard superior prepares to be confronted

blocks.note: a square is a stuffy, conventional person, an old diehard
sup. is the dictionary abbreviation for superior

explanation.surface: A stubborn boss braces for a confrontation.
explanation.definitionFit: To square up is to adopt a fighting stance, readying oneself for an opponent's challenge.

clue.text: Sense nameless things at sea

indicators.note: without a name means the abbreviation for name, N, is dropped
being at sea means confused and adrift, so the letters are disordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: One perceives unnamed objects out on the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: Sight is one of the five senses, so the sense of seeing fits the bare word.

clue.text: The science of looking after number one?

definitions.text: The science of looking after number one?

blocks.clueFragment: The science of looking after number one?
blocks.note: surface reading: the study of selfishness, putting oneself first
setter's reading: number one is a childish word for passing water, so this is the medical field of the urinary tract

explanation.walkthrough: Looking after number one means being selfish; but children call a wee number one, so the science is the medical speciality of the waterworks.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical specialism treats the urinary system, which handles urine, nursery slang number one.

clue.text: Criminal caterer casually nicks last two pieces of cake

indicators.note: done casually, without care, so the letters fall out of order
pieces are letters here, and the last two come off the end
to nick is to steal, so one piece takes the other into itself

blocks.note: taken as written
the final two letters of cake

explanation.surface: A dishonest caterer pinches the last bits of cake.
explanation.definitionFit: A racketeer runs dishonest schemes for profit, making them a criminal.

clue.text: Unsympathetic treatment of husband after trousers split

indicators.note: one item coming after another sets which is written first

blocks.note: short trousers
H is the abbreviation for husband
a rift is a split or breach

explanation.surface: A husband gets no sympathy after splitting his trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: Short shrift means curt, dismissive treatment that gives little attention or sympathy.

clue.text: Boozer brought up halfhearted belch

indicators.note: the heart is the middle, and half of it goes, so one of the two central letters is lost
in a down entry, bringing something up means writing it bottom to top

blocks.note: a burp is a belch

explanation.surface: A drinker brought up a feeble burp.
explanation.walkthrough: Boozer looks like the drinker; in British slang it is the pub itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Boozer is British slang for a public house, a place where alcohol is drunk.

clue.text: Two companies start to advertise beverage

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: CO, the abbreviation for company, twice
the opening letter of advertise

explanation.surface: A pair of firms begin marketing a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Cocoa is a hot chocolate drink, so it is one example of a beverage.

clue.text: No gentleman originally entered The Apprentice

indicators.note: originally means at the origin, so each word's first letter is used

blocks.note: a cad is a man who behaves dishonourably
the opening letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A rotter appeared on the TV business show The Apprentice.
explanation.walkthrough: The Apprentice is a reality TV contest, but the capital hides a plain noun: a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadet is a trainee, especially in the forces or police, so a kind of apprentice.

clue.text: Alcott novel entertaining single singer

indicators.note: novel means new, so the name is remade in a fresh order
a host entertaining a guest has them inside the house

blocks.note: taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A Louisa May Alcott book features a solo vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: Novel looks like a book by Alcott, but it is an adjective meaning new. Singer is a songbird.
explanation.definitionFit: The coal tit is a small songbird of the tit family, and crosswords often call birds singers.

clue.text: We gather supermarket chain conceals volatile fluids

indicators.note: we gather means we hear it said, so the sound counts rather than the spelling

blocks.note: Aldi is a discount supermarket chain, and hides means conceals

explanation.surface: We hear a supermarket is hiding flammable liquids.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldehydes, such as formaldehyde and acetaldehyde, are organic compounds, many of them volatile liquids.

clue.text: King George with pained expression over unserious brother

blocks.note: Georgius Rex, the royal cipher
what one says when hurt
O is the cricket scoring abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A grimacing monarch frowns at a frivolous sibling.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket an over is a set of six balls, abbreviated O on scorecards.
explanation.definitionFit: Groucho was one of the Marx Brothers, the comedy act, hence a far from serious sibling.

clue.text: Entice posh girl back in the direction of lovemaking spot

definitions.text: in the direction of lovemaking spot

indicators.note: going back means the whole string is read from the end towards the start

blocks.note: to draw someone in is to lure them
a debutante, a upper-class young woman entering society

explanation.surface: Luring a society girl back towards the bedroom.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedward is an adverb meaning towards bed, and bed is where lovers make love.

clue.text: Figure of speech in tense Hitchcock thriller

blocks.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense
Rope is a 1948 Hitchcock film

explanation.surface: A rhetorical device found in a suspenseful Hitchcock film.
explanation.definitionFit: A trope is a rhetorical figure, a word or expression used in a non-literal sense.

clue.text: Output of sewer covers church after boob

indicators.note: one item following another fixes the order the two are written in

blocks.note: tops are lids or covers
slang for a breast
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: Waste from the drains covers a church after a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: The sewer is not a drain but someone who sews; boob reads as a mistake but here is the slang body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Topstitching is visible decorative stitching on a garment's surface, produced by a person sewing.

clue.text: Clip of lover exercising intimate muscles

indicators.note: exercising involves stretching and moving about, so the letters are worked into new places

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Video footage of a partner working out private muscles.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is also an &lit-style joke: such exercises are known for tightening those muscles.
explanation.definitionFit: This muscle group supports the bladder and bowel and is involved in sexual function, hence intimate.

clue.text: Chief of Police twisted your nose

indicators.note: the chief of a word is its head, the letter at the front
twisted round, the short abbreviation runs the other way

blocks.note: the leading letter of police
YR is a common written abbreviation of your

explanation.surface: A police chief has bent your nose out of shape.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose, as a verb, is to snoop into others' affairs, the same idea as to pry.

clue.text: Teacher eager to stop right after class

indicators.note: a stopper plugs a gap, so this piece is placed inside another
following another item fixes which piece is written first

blocks.note: physical education, a school lesson
agog means keenly expectant
what is due to you is your right

explanation.surface: A keen pupil wants to halt immediately after a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedagogue is a schoolteacher, often a strict or pedantic one.

clue.text: Intoxicated dahlia expert recklessly snubbing prince

indicators.note: acting recklessly suggests wild disorder, so these letters get jumbled
to snub someone is to cut them, so that letter is left out

blocks.note: taken as written
P is the abbreviation for prince

explanation.surface: A drunken gardener who specialises in dahlias cold-shoulders royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Intoxicated can mean thrilled or elated, as in intoxicated by success, which is exactly exhilarated.

clue.text: Romeo isn't commonly pursuing tranquillity or moderation

indicators.note: to pursue is to come behind, so this pair follows the other piece

blocks.note: rest is peace and calm
R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the colloquial or dialect form of isn't

explanation.surface: Romeo is not, in the vernacular, chasing calm or self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: Restraint is self-control or holding back from excess, which is moderation.

clue.text: Branches out and writes poetry after first couple of divorces

indicators.note: a couple is two, taken from the front of the word
following something means it is written to the right of that piece

blocks.note: the opening pair of letters of divorces
to versify is to compose verse

explanation.surface: Someone expands their interests and turns to verse after a pair of failed marriages.
explanation.definitionFit: To diversify is to extend activity into new areas, which is to branch out.

clue.text: One adopting habit without drama or harm

indicators.note: without means lacking, so that piece is taken away

blocks.note: a novice in a religious order, who has taken the habit
No, or Noh, is the classical Japanese drama

explanation.surface: Someone takes up a habit without fuss or damage.
explanation.walkthrough: Habit reads as a routine but is the robe of a nun or monk, so one adopting it is a novice.
explanation.definitionFit: To vitiate is to spoil or impair the quality of something, a formal word for harm.

clue.text: Chap's partially bewhiskered

indicators.note: only part of the next word is used, a run of consecutive letters within it

blocks.note: the letters sit inside this word

explanation.surface: A man is somewhat whiskery.
explanation.definitionFit: Chap's means belonging to a man, and the possessive pronoun for that is the masculine one.

clue.text: Straight answers about Irish courtesan

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pair goes round the other piece

blocks.note: slang short for heterosexual
A for answer, twice
IR is a standard abbreviation for Irish

explanation.surface: Frank replies concerning an Irish mistress.
explanation.definitionFit: A hetaira was a cultivated courtesan in ancient Greece, a high-class companion.

clue.text: Photograph junk

blocks.note: first meaning: to obtain a picture of something
second meaning: British slang for getting rid of something

explanation.walkthrough: Get shot of is British slang for get rid of; read literally, getting a shot of something is taking its picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase works literally as capturing an image and idiomatically as throwing something away.

clue.text: Core of our planet getting hot going forward

indicators.note: the letter for hot moves forward from the back to the front of the word

blocks.note: the planet we live on

explanation.surface: The centre of the world grows hotter in future.
explanation.walkthrough: H for hot is a standard abbreviation, as on taps.
explanation.definitionFit: The heart of something is its centre or most vital part, which is its core.

clue.text: Heard unfortunate gag

indicators.note: something heard is caught by the ear, so the sound counts, not the spelling

blocks.note: a wretch is an unfortunate person

explanation.surface: Someone heard a joke that fell flat.
explanation.walkthrough: Gag wants to be a joke; it is the verb for heaving.
explanation.definitionFit: To gag is to choke or heave as if about to vomit, which is to retch.

clue.text: Sweetheart sounding like Attila?

indicators.note: sounding like means the word matches in speech, not on the page

blocks.note: Attila was leader of the Huns, so something like him would be Hun-y

explanation.surface: A lover is described as rather like the warlike king of the Huns.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags a made-up word: like a Hun, said out loud, matches the term of endearment.
explanation.definitionFit: Honey is an affectionate term of address for a loved one, like sweetheart.

clue.text: Llama manure enthralling leaders of agricultural co-operative

indicators.note: to enthrall is to hold captive, so one piece holds the other inside it
leaders are those at the front, so only initial letters count

blocks.note: guano is bird or bat droppings used as fertiliser
initials of the two words

explanation.surface: Farm co-op bosses are captivated by animal dung.
explanation.definitionFit: The guanaco is a wild South American camelid of the llama family, so it is a llama in the broad sense.

clue.text: King of Mercia, mostly bad

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: Offa was an eighth-century king of Mercia, the Anglo-Saxon kingdom

explanation.surface: An old English king who was largely wicked.
explanation.walkthrough: Mercia was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom in the English Midlands; Offa built the dyke on the Welsh border.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that has gone off is bad, spoiled and no longer fit to eat.

clue.text: Tear-jerker full of sanctimonious sentiment

indicators.note: something full of another thing has it inside

blocks.note: chopping an onion makes the eyes water
pi is short for pious, sanctimonious

explanation.surface: A weepy film awash with preachy sentimentality.
explanation.walkthrough: Tear-jerker suggests a sad film, but here it is the vegetable that makes you cry.
explanation.definitionFit: A sentiment is a view or attitude held about something, which is an opinion.

clue.text: Pass motion in futile gesture

indicators.note: the letters are located in the run of text that follows

blocks.note: spans the end of futile and the start of gesture

explanation.surface: Proposing a motion with a pointless gesture, as in a debate.
explanation.walkthrough: Pass motion reads like a debating vote; it is the bodily sense of evacuating the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: To egest is to discharge waste from the body, which is the medical sense of passing a motion.

clue.text: White House occupant shaking lardy fist

indicators.note: shaking something jumbles it up, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in the presidential residence waves a chubby fist.
explanation.definitionFit: The President's spouse, known by this title, lives at the presidential residence in Washington.
